ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is an observation tower $EF$ at the top $E$ of a mountain. It is known that the angle $\angle EAB$ between the mountain slope and the horizontal plane is $30^\circ$, the height of the mountain $EB$ is 120 meters, point $C$ is 180 meters away from the base of the mountain $A$, $CD\parallel AB$, and intersects $EB$ at point $D$. The elevation angle $\angle FCD$ of the top end $F$ of the observation tower measured at point $C$ is $60^\circ$. What is the height of the observation tower $EF$ in meters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the question, we have: $\angle ABE=90^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle EAB=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEB=60^\circ$, $AE=2EB$, \\
$\because$ $EB=120$, \\
$\therefore$ $AE=2EB=240$, \\
$\because$ $AC=180$, \\
$\therefore$ $CE=AE-AC=60$, \\
$\because$ $CD\parallel AB$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CDE=\angle ABE=90^\circ$, $\angle ECD=\angle EAB=30^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle FCD=60^\circ$, $\angle FCE=\angle FCD-\angle ECD=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle FCE=\angle CFE=30^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $EF=CE=60$, \\
thus, the height of the tower is \boxed{60} meters.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/trigonometric route. Read from the diagram that AB can be taken as a horizontal x-axis, EB and EF are vertical on the same line through B/E, C lies on the slope AE, and CD is horizontal from C to the vertical through E. From the text, ∠EAB=30°, EB=120 m, AC=180 m, and ∠FCD=60°. Put A=(0,0) and let AB be the x-axis. Since E is 120 m above the base and AE makes a 30° angle with the horizontal, AB=120/tan30°=120√3, so E=(120√3,120). Since AC=180 along the same 30° slope, C=(180cos30°,180sin30°)=(90√3,90). Let the tower height be EF=h, so F=(120√3,120+h). From C to F, the horizontal difference is 120√3−90√3=30√3 and the vertical difference is 120+h−90=h+30. The elevation angle ∠FCD is 60° above the horizontal CD, so tan60°=(h+30)/(30√3). Thus √3=(h+30)/(30√3), giving h+30=90 and h=60 m.

再推理：取 A=(0,0)，令 AB 为 x 轴。因为 AE 与水平夹角为 30°，且 E 到地面的高度 EB=120，所以点 E 的纵坐标是 120。由 tan30°=EB/AB=120/AB，得 AB=120/ tan30°=120√3，因此 E=(120√3,120)。

C 在斜坡 AE 上，并且 AC=180，沿 30° 方向分解坐标，得 C=(180cos30°,180sin30°)=(90√3,90)。

设观测塔 EF 的高度为 h，则 F=(120√3,120+h)。从 C 到 F 的水平距离为 120√3-90√3=30√3，竖直距离为 (120+h)-90=h+30。由于 CD 是水平线，所以 ∠FCD=60° 表示 CF 与水平夹角为 60°，因此 tan60°=(h+30)/(30√3)。

因为 tan60°=√3，所以 √3=(h+30)/(30√3)，即 h+30=90，故 h=60。

再推理：取 A=(0,0)，令 AB 为 x 轴。因为 AE 与水平夹角为 30°，且 E 到地面的高度 EB=120，所以点 E 的纵坐标是 120。由 tan30°=EB/AB=120/AB，得 AB=120/ tan30°=120√3，因此 E=(120√3,120)。

C 在斜坡 AE 上，并且 AC=180，沿 30° 方向分解坐标，得 C=(180cos30°,180sin30°)=(90√3,90)。

设观测塔 EF 的高度为 h，则 F=(120√3,120+h)。从 C 到 F 的水平距离为 120√3-90√3=30√3，竖直距离为 (120+h)-90=h+30。由于 CD 是水平线，所以 ∠FCD=60° 表示 CF 与水平夹角为 60°，因此 tan60°=(h+30)/(30√3)。

因为 tan60°=√3，所以 √3=(h+30)/(30√3)，即 h+30=90，故 h=60。

planner_metadata.text_role: The text provides the measurable inputs: mountain height EB=120 m, slope angle 30°, distance AC=180 m, CD∥AB, and elevation angle ∠FCD=60°.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use coordinate geometry, basic trigonometric definitions for sin, cos, and tangent, and the tangent relation for an angle of elevation.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, there is an observation tower $EF$ at the top $E$ of a mountain. It is known that the angle $\angle EAB$ between the mountain slope and the horizontal plane is $30^\circ$, the height of the mountain $EB$ is 120 meters, point $C$ is 180 meters away from the base of the mountain $A$, $CD\parallel AB$, and intersects $EB$ at point $D$. The elevation angle $\angle FCD$ of the top end $F$ of the observation tower measured at point $C$ is $60^\circ$. What is the height of the observation tower $EF$ in meters?
raw_record.answer:
According to the question, we have: $\angle ABE=90^\circ$, 
$\because$ $\angle EAB=30^\circ$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle AEB=60^\circ$, $AE=2EB$, 
$\because$ $EB=120$, 
$\therefore$ $AE=2EB=240$, 
$\because$ $AC=180$, 
$\therefore$ $CE=AE-AC=60$, 
$\because$ $CD\parallel AB$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle CDE=\angle ABE=90^\circ$, $\angle ECD=\angle EAB=30^\circ$, 
$\because$ $\angle FCD=60^\circ$, $\angle FCE=\angle FCD-\angle ECD=30^\circ$, 
$\therefore$ $\angle FCE=\angle CFE=30^\circ$, 
$\therefore$ $EF=CE=60$, 
thus, the height of the tower is $\boxed{60}$ meters.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, A and B are on the same horizontal straight line, there is a right-angle mark at B, EB is a vertical dashed line upward from B, and E is on the slope oblique line AE; C is on the oblique line AE and is between A and E; from C, draw a horizontal dashed line CD to the right, intersecting the vertical line EB at D; EF is a vertical tower upward from E, F is directly above E, and C and F are connected.

Then reason: From the figure, it can be seen that triangle ABE is right-angled at B, that is, ∠ABE=90°. The problem gives ∠EAB=30°, so triangle ABE is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle. EB=120 m and EB corresponds to the 30° angle, so the hypotenuse AE=2×EB=240 m. Also because C is on AE, AC=180 m, so CE=AE−AC=240−180=60 m. Since CD∥AB, CD is a horizontal line, therefore ∠ECD equals the angle between the slope and the horizontal line, ∠EAB, that is, ∠ECD=30°. The problem gives ∠FCD=60°, so ∠FCE=∠FCD−∠ECD=60°−30°=30°. In triangle CEF, CE is in the direction of the slope, and EF is in the vertical direction, therefore ∠CEF=120°, hence ∠CFE=180°−120°−30°=30°. Thus ∠FCE=∠CFE, and the sides opposite them are equal, so EF=CE=60 m.
